R-60 does not appear in this value, so using it would invent an identifier. The worker's own R01 rule applies: the target is the thing named, not what that thing concerns.
Same referent as act.target: the motion. Coding it WP-7B-R1 would pair it with R04's norm (ENGINEERING START-EXECUTION WP-7B-R1), which is about something else.

In the same record, act.target codes this motion as R-60 and norm.about_target codes it as WP-7B-R1. The value names the motion without its identifier, so the target is UNMAPPABLE, not the work package.

The target is the PO's 'three state planes' framing of O-CLOSURE-VOCAB, not O-CLOSURE-VOCAB itself. A framing is a view of the thing, not a part of it. This is the same situation as R01, where the worker coded 'the ambiguity over ... R-81..R-85' as UNMAPPABLE.

'ANNOTATE is adopted' means the Chief chose the ANNOTATE disposition inside R-94. It is not the adoption of a ruling. In R01 the worker separated ADOPT (adopting a ruling) from other kinds of 'adopt'. Coding ADOPT here creates an 'ARB-CHIEF ADOPT' act, which conflicts with R01 and R02, where only the Decision Authority adopts rulings. That conflict is manufactured.

caveats: Usable only with conditions: after the 16 corrections, no pairing on these codes creates a false match or contrast, provided the consumer (a) carries norm modality/polarity separately, (b) expands composite targets into their members, and (c) orders records in time.

The worker codes norm.about_operation without its modality (permitted / forbidden / not authorized): R12, R14, R20–R22, R26, R27, R31, R33. That is fine for a vocabulary, but pairing on operation alone would treat real time sequences as contradictions (R14 or R31 'not authorized' vs R32 or R34 'authorized'; R10 'does not begin' vs the R11 WP-4B RED commit).

Composite targets (R02, R14, R36) break the 'one canonical identifier' rule. There is no single right member to choose, so they are left as is. Note that 'R-81 and R-84' (R36) is a conjunction the worker built; the identifiers are in the value but the string is not.

UNMAPPABLE is used honestly throughout. R05 norm.about_operation ('plan and implement') is correctly UNMAPPABLE because PLAN and START-EXECUTION must not be merged, but R05 therefore drops out of plan/execute pairings with R12.
